metadata.title: Random But True: The Real Story of Laika, the Space Dog
metadata.caption:
For 45 years, the Soviet Union told the world this dog died peacefully in space. She didn't.

Laika was a stray picked up off the streets of Moscow, launched aboard Sputnik 2 on November 3, 1957 - the first living creature to ever orbit the Earth.

Officials claimed she survived for days before a painless death. In 2002, one of the mission's own scientists finally admitted the truth: she died within hours, when a fault in the capsule's cooling system caused it to overheat.

The spacecraft was never built to bring her home either way - but the official story was still a lie for 45 years.
